record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Appendix C's CIFAR-10 result figures are included without readable descriptions or values.
record.tranche_reason: Compares normalization methods during CIFAR-10 classifier training and reports training accuracy/loss outcomes across learning rates; this is a conceptual test of V6's training-speed claim, using learned normalization methods rather than simply adding batch normalization.
record.gate_note: The paper reports CIFAR-10 classifier results for Batch Normalization, learned DWCK normalization, and learned-statistics normalization. Its explicit text gives comparative results but no exact accuracy or loss values. Figure captions identify training and validation curves, but the included plots do not provide readable numeric values.
record.test_reason: Batch normalization serves as a benchmark for proposed normalization methods. The readable results compare these methods' accuracy, loss and stability with BN; they do not establish that adding BN speeds accuracy gains or increases learning-rate tolerance relative to the same network without normalization. The plain classifier appears in figure captions, but its relevant training trajectories cannot be read from the supplied text.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' claims. The conclusion specifically says learned weighted-sum normalization can match BN on CIFAR-10 and improve convergence. Elsewhere, the authors claim learned-statistics normalization can sometimes rival or exceed BN with fewer learnable parameters. These are claims about their proposed methods, rather than a demonstrated BN-versus-no-normalization acceleration effect.
record.recipe_differences: Tests newly proposed learned DWCK and learned-statistics normalization against Batch Normalization on ALL-CNN-C; it does not reproduce the claim's BN addition comparison across the model and dataset set named in V6.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning-rate range and batch size change the reported comparison; learned-statistics normalization's validation accuracy lags BN at [10−5, 10−3], while it initially exceeds BN at [0.05, 0.01]. DWCK results are reported as comparable at batch sizes 256, 128, and 64, and superior and more stable at batch sizes 32 and 16 for most tried learning rates.

fits_no_version.finding: At low learning rates, learned-statistics normalization has validation accuracy below BN but above the plain classifier.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learned-statistics normalization can improve validation accuracy over an unnormalized ALL-CNN-C classifier on CIFAR-10.

fits_no_version.finding: Learned-statistics normalization initially exceeds BN in validation accuracy and has lower, less oscillating loss in the reported higher-learning-rate setting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learned-statistics normalization can outperform BN during ALL-CNN-C training under some learning-rate choices.

fits_no_version.finding: DWCK performs comparably to BN at batch sizes 64–256 and is described as superior and more stable at batch sizes 16 and 32 for most tested learning rates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The relative performance of DWCK and BN depends on batch size and learning rate.

record.problems: No exact numeric accuracy or loss results are stated in the readable text; the relevant figures are supplied without extractable numeric values. The metric behind the Section 4 'superior and more stable' comparison is not specified in that statement. No uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results omitted. Appendix C consists of figures without readable result values in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error, including random or corrupted labels, and dependence on model size or training recipe.
Teacher-student spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Training degradation with depth, identity shortcuts, and the specified deep-network alternatives.
Comparative effects of initialization on training speed, signal propagation and trainable depth.
Loss and curvature dynamics relative to the initial or evolving stability threshold.

BN-induced acceleration and higher learning-rate tolerance relative to the same unnormalized network; Fixup's speed and stability without normalization. Relevant BN-versus-plain trajectories cannot be determined from the supplied figures.

record.verdict_notes: Alternative normalization outperforming BN does not challenge V6: V6 does not claim BN is optimal among normalization methods. The unreadable figure trajectories and ambiguous color descriptions prevent recovering a direct BN-versus-plain training-speed result.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label or corrupted-label experiment, model-size sweep, or claim about reaching zero training classification error is reported.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student problem or width comparison is reported.
No depth comparison involving plain networks and identity shortcuts is reported.
No initialization comparison or signal/gradient propagation measurement is reported.
No stability-threshold or above-threshold learning-rate experiment is reported.

Tests CIFAR-10 classification with ALL-CNN-C and compares normalization methods at stated learning rates; it does not test sigmoid MNIST, VGG CIFAR-10, Inception ImageNet, higher learning-rate tolerance directly, or Fixup.

rows.subject: ALL-CNN with BN
rows.size_stated: 96 filters in initial layers; 192 filters in later layers as described for the ALL-CNN-C classifier
rows.operation_detail: Train CIFAR-10 classifier with Batch Normalization; compare its validation accuracy with learned-statistics CNN normalization.
rows.measure: Validation accuracy relative to plain classifier and learned-statistics normalization.
rows.value: The learned-statistics normalization does not match the validation accuracy of Batch Normalization, yet makes gains with respect to the plain classifier.
rows.note: One comparative outcome is stated for the learning-rate range; no exact accuracy values are given.
rows.check: Validation-accuracy ordering does not establish V6's training-speed effect. The stated ordering is BN above learned-statistics normalization above the plain classifier. Figure 4 specifies an example at learning rate 0.0001 for 50 epochs.

rows.subject: ALL-CNN with one-dimensional CNN learned-statistics normalization
rows.size_stated: 96 filters in initial layers; 192 filters in later layers as described for the ALL-CNN-C classifier
rows.operation_detail: Train CIFAR-10 classifier with learned mean and standard-deviation statistics networks; compare validation accuracy and loss with Batch Normalization.
rows.measure: Validation accuracy compared with Batch Normalization.
rows.value: Initially out performs Batch Normalization when it comes to validation accuracy; accuracy is noticibly higher than Batch Normalization for the first 25 epochs.
rows.note: The text says the learned method leads early; it does not state the final accuracy difference or provide exact values.
rows.check: This measures the proposed method against BN, rather than BN's benefit over no normalization or Fixup's performance. Figure 5 specifies learning rate 0.025 and 75 epochs; the prose describes a broader range of 0.01–0.05.

rows.subject: ALL-CNN with one-dimensional CNN learned-statistics normalization
rows.size_stated: 96 filters in initial layers; 192 filters in later layers as described for the ALL-CNN-C classifier
rows.operation_detail: Train CIFAR-10 classifier with learned mean and standard-deviation statistics networks; compare loss with Batch Normalization.
rows.measure: Training and validation loss compared with Batch Normalization.
rows.value: The loss of the CNN normalization is lower and less oscillating than Batch Normalization throughtout the duration of the training.
rows.note: The comparison is explicitly stated, but no exact loss values are supplied.
rows.check: Lower and less oscillating loss for another normalization method relative to BN does not test a named version. Figure 6 specifies learning rate 0.025 and 75 epochs.

rows.subject: ALL-CNN with BN
rows.size_stated: 96 filters in initial layers; 192 filters in later layers as described for the ALL-CNN-C classifier
rows.operation_detail: Train CIFAR-10 classifier with Batch Normalization and compare results with learned DWCK normalization.
rows.measure: Comparative classifier results; metric not specified in this statement.
rows.value: The results for ALL-CNN with BN and ALL-CNN with DWCK were comparable.
rows.note: The comparison names no specific metric, so it does not establish accuracy gain or training speed on its own.
rows.check: An unspecified performance comparison between BN and DWCK does not measure V6's BN-versus-unnormalized training-speed effect. The implemented DWCK method uses ordinary standard deviation because weighted standard deviation was computationally unstable.

rows.subject: ALL-CNN with DWCK
rows.size_stated: 96 filters in initial layers; 192 filters in later layers as described for the ALL-CNN-C classifier
rows.operation_detail: Train CIFAR-10 classifier using learned depth-wise convolutional normalization; compare with Batch Normalization.
rows.measure: Comparative performance and stability; specific metric not stated.
rows.value: For most of the learning rates for batch sizes of 32 and 16 ALL-CNN with DWCK resulted superior and more stable.
rows.note: The statement is qualified to most tried learning rates and small batch sizes; the exact performance metric is not identified here.
rows.check: Superior and more stable DWCK performance relative to BN is a result about the proposed method, with no specific metric supplied here. It does not establish BN's speed or learning-rate benefit over an unnormalized network. DWCK used ordinary standard deviation.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
